title: Face with Diagonal Mouth Emoji 🫤 Meaning: The “Meh” Face
description: The face with diagonal mouth emoji 🫤 means meh, unsure, unimpressed or quietly skeptical. See when this 2021 emoji's slanted mouth says more than a shrug.
summary: The 🫤 face with diagonal mouth means meh. It expresses lukewarm feelings: not impressed, not convinced, not sure, a bit let down. The straight slanted mouth sits between a frown and a neutral line, so it suits reactions that are negative but too mild or too uncertain for a stronger face.
meaning: Some reactions are hard to put into words because there is so little to them. The movie was fine. The plan might work. The apology was technically an apology. 🫤 exists for these. Its mouth, a single line tilted up at one end, matches the sideways twist people make when they are weighing something and finding it lacking.

Skepticism is one of its main uses. Sent after a promise or a sales pitch, it says I will believe it when I see it. It is less confrontational than the raised eyebrow face. The sender is not demanding proof, just declining to get excited. It also covers plain indecision, as when asked to choose between two options that seem equally fine.

It is also a face of mild disappointment and resignation. Plans that fell through, a gift that missed, a result that was merely okay: 🫤 acknowledges the letdown and signals the sender will not make a fuss. Paired with oh well or I guess, it has a shrugging, whatever tone that younger users in particular favor.

Approved in Unicode 14.0 in 2021, it arrived to sit beside the older confused face, whose curved frown reads as sadder. The new emoji is drier. It is also less familiar than long-established faces, and at small sizes the mouth can be mistaken for a smirk, so some recipients may need context.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: It answers how was it when the truth is unremarkable. It also responds to suggestions you are not keen on without rejecting them outright, which makes it a diplomatic no. If a friend sends it about your plan, they are open to alternatives and waiting for you to offer one.

contexts.label: From a partner or crush
contexts.body: It usually means they are underwhelmed or unsure, and that deserves a follow-up. After you propose a date idea, 🫤 says not really my thing. After a disagreement, it says the matter is not settled for them, even if they have stopped arguing.

contexts.label: On social media
contexts.body: Reviews, reaction posts and replies to announcements use it for a lukewarm verdict. It is common under trailers, product reveals and sports signings that fans find uninspiring. It conveys that expectations were not met, in a tone closer to a sigh than a complaint.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: It is an honest but soft way to express reservations about a proposal or timeline. It tells colleagues you have doubts while leaving room for discussion. Since it is vague by nature, add a sentence about what concerns you so the feedback can be acted on.

examples.text: How was the date? — It was fine 🫤
examples.meaning: Underwhelming; nothing went wrong but there was no spark.

examples.text: He says he'll pay me back Friday 🫤
examples.meaning: Doubtful that the promise will be kept.

examples.text: Pizza or tacos? I don't know 🫤
examples.meaning: Undecided and without a strong preference.

examples.text: Got a gift card to a store I never go to 🫤
examples.meaning: Mildly disappointed but trying to be gracious.

examples.text: I guess we could go there 🫤
examples.meaning: Reluctant agreement; they would prefer something else.

combos.meaning: Meh, whatever; no strong opinion and no enthusiasm.
Thought about it and still unconvinced.

confusedWith.difference: 😕 has a curved, lopsided frown and reads as puzzled or a little hurt. 🫤 has a straight slanted mouth and reads as skeptical or indifferent. The older face is softer; the newer one is drier.
😐 has a perfectly level mouth and shows no reaction at all, often deadpan annoyance. 🫤 tilts the line, which adds doubt or dissatisfaction. Neutral says nothing; diagonal says not great.
😏 curls up at one side with sly, knowing eyes and suggests smugness or flirting. 🫤 has plain round eyes and no smile at all. The slants can look alike at a glance, but the moods are opposite.

avoid: Do not use it in response to something a person is clearly proud of unless you want to deflate them.
Avoid it as your only reply to an invitation, since it leaves the host unsure whether you are coming.
Skip it when you have a strong objection; it will be read as minor.
design: A yellow face with simple open eyes and a mouth drawn as a short straight line slanting diagonally. There are no eyebrows on most designs. Vendors follow the same basic drawing, with only small differences in the angle and length of the line, so it looks much the same on every platform that supports it.

faqs.a: It means the sender feels lukewarm, doubtful or mildly disappointed. Think of it as a typed meh or a hmm, not sure. It is deliberately low-key, so the surrounding words usually tell you which shade is intended.

faqs.q: What does 🫤 mean from a guy or girl?
faqs.a: That they are not thrilled or not convinced by what was just said. It does not mean anger. If it follows your suggestion, offer another option. If it follows your explanation, they probably still have doubts.

Mildly. It sits on the negative side of neutral, expressing reservations, skepticism or a small letdown. It is far gentler than an eye roll or an angry face, and is often chosen to avoid sounding harsh.

faqs.q: When did the diagonal mouth emoji come out?
faqs.a: It was approved in Unicode 14.0 in 2021, alongside the melting face, the saluting face, the dotted line face and the face holding back tears. Devices that have not been updated since then may show it as a blank box.
